It is fixed in Go 1.26.9 and 1.27.2 for the HTTP/2 implementation in net/http, and in golang.org/x/net v0.60.0 for golang.org/x/net/http2: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6611, https://github.com/golang/go/issues/81742, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/U2fTuyDJznI. The golang.org/x/net fix is https://github.com/golang/net/commit/cc7d34fd2dd5864bcafe3e5e0a84919240be98c0, and for Go 1.26 it is in https://github.com/golang/go/commit/6e049521882c944afc1e519a83971ec421dc2974 on release-branch.go1.26, first released in Go 1.26.9; both name CVE-2026-78669 and add a connection-level connOutflow type. We read every alertmanager-dev package published for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository, x86_64 and aarch64: 36 versions, 0.31.1-r0 to the current 0.35.0-r2, each matching its repository index checksum. Each package holds two files, the Go programs /usr/bin/alertmanager and /usr/bin/amtool, and in every build both programs, on both architectures, carry the same Go and module versions. For every program we read the Go build information and the function table (pclntab), which contains runtime.main in every program. Both programs in every build link functions the Go vulnerability database lists for both packages, for example net/http.(*http2Framer).WriteSettings and golang.org/x/net/http2.(*Framer).WriteSettings and (*clientConnReadLoop).processSettingsNoWrite, so the status follows the versions. Builds 0.31.1-r0 to 0.34.1-r1 are built with Go 1.25.7 or 1.26.1 to 1.26.8 and embed golang.org/x/net v0.49.0 to v0.59.0, so they lack both fixes. 0.34.1-r2 is the first build with Go 1.26.9 and golang.org/x/net v0.61.0, and every later build uses Go 1.26.9 to 1.26.11 and golang.org/x/net v0.61.0 or v0.62.0. No build uses Go 1.27 or replaces golang.org/x/net. As a check on the boundary, a byte search finds the connOutflow type name in both programs of 0.34.1-r2 and every later build, and in no program of 0.34.1-r1 or any earlier build, on both architectures. The range ends at 0.34.1-r2.

CVE-2026-78669 (GO-2026-6611): a malicious HTTP/2 peer can cause excessive CPU consumption in a client or server built on net/http or golang.org/x/net/http2 by opening many streams and then sending many small SETTINGS frames that change SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE. It is fixed in Go 1.26.9 and 1.27.2 for net/http, and in golang.org/x/net v0.60.0 for golang.org/x/net/http2: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6611, https://go.dev/issue/81742, https://go.dev/cl/847186, https://go.dev/cl/847308 and, for the Go 1.26 release branch, https://go.dev/cl/847111, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/U2fTuyDJznI, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/ZPwCyRUuGBs. Read the Go build information and the function table (with a reader of the Go symbol table that also works on stripped binaries) of every build-dev package published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository: 90 builds, 2.6.4-r0 through the current 2.29.1-r2, each for x86_64 and aarch64 except 2.6.4-r0, which is published for aarch64 only; every download was checked against the index checksum. Version 2.19.1-r1 is listed three times in each index; the repository serves one copy, which matches one of those entries' checksum, and that copy was read. Each package holds one file, the Go program /usr/bin/build. runtime.main is in its function table in every build, so every table was read. In every build, /usr/bin/build links net/http functions the advisory names, including (*Transport).RoundTrip, and golang.org/x/net/http2 functions it names, including (*Framer).ReadFrame and (*Framer).WriteSettings. Builds before 2.26.0-r1 are built with Go 1.25.7 to 1.26.8; 2.26.0-r1 is built with Go 1.26.9 but carries golang.org/x/net 0.58.0, and every build before 2.26.0-r2 carries golang.org/x/net 0.47.0 to 0.59.0 in the programs that link golang.org/x/net/http2. From 2.26.0-r2 on, every Go program is built with Go 1.26.9 to 1.26.11, and every program that links golang.org/x/net/http2 carries golang.org/x/net 0.60.0 to 0.62.0. No build uses Go 1.27.

Read every published alloy package for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository: 44 builds, 1.18.1-0 to the current 1.22.0-16, for amd64 and arm64 (1.21.2-0 is published for arm64 only), 87 packages, each checked against the index SHA256; no debug-symbol package is published for this source. Each package installs /usr/bin/alloy, its only ELF program, plus the default configuration /etc/alloy/config.alloy and an SPDX SBOM JSON file under /opt/docker/sbom. Both architectures of a build carry the same Go and module versions, and no build replaces the module. In every package, the function symbols of /usr/bin/alloy (go tool nm) include the standard library's HTTP/2 server and client SETTINGS handling (the serverConn processSettingInitialWindowSize and clientConnReadLoop processSettingsNoWrite methods, in net/http before Go 1.27 and in net/http/internal/http2 from Go 1.27), and golang.org/x/net/http2 is linked as well, so the vulnerable code is present. The Go version by build is 1.18.1-0: 1.26.6; 1.18.1-1 to 1.19.2-2: 1.26.7; 1.19.2-3 to 1.20.1-1: 1.26.8; 1.20.1-2 and 1.20.1-3: 1.26.9; 1.21.0-0: 1.27.2; 1.21.0-1 to 1.21.3-2: 1.27.3; 1.21.3-3 to 1.22.0-16: 1.27.4. golang.org/x/net is v0.58.0 in 1.18.1-0 to 1.19.2-3 and v0.59.0 in 1.19.2-4 to 1.20.1-1, and v0.60.0 or later from 1.20.1-2. The range ends at 1.20.1-2, the first build with both Go 1.26.9 or later and golang.org/x/net v0.60.0 or later.

CVE-2026-78669 (GO-2026-6611): a malicious HTTP/2 peer could cause excessive CPU consumption in a client or server by opening many streams and then sending many small SETTINGS frames that change SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE, because each change walked every open stream. Go 1.27.2 fixes net/http/internal/http2, Go 1.26.9 fixes the 1.26 line, and golang.org/x/net v0.60.0 fixes the golang.org/x/net/http2 module (https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6611, https://go.dev/issue/81742, https://go.dev/cl/847186, https://go.dev/cl/847308, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/U2fTuyDJznI, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/ZPwCyRUuGBs). On release-branch.go1.27, which the Go 1.27 releases are cut from, the fix is commit 1d58cdaa1069 (https://go.dev/cl/847031), released in Go 1.27.2. This package is the Go 1.27 toolchain, and its version is the Go release it packages. We inspected every published golang-1.27-dev package for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository, amd64 and arm64, from 1.27.0-0 to the current 1.27.4-18; each build's go command reports the Go release in its package version. In net/http/internal/http2 (src/net/http/internal/http2/flow.go), the builds below 1.27.2-0 (1.27.0-0 to 1.27.1-1) package Go releases before 1.27.2 and adjust and check the flow-control window of every open stream on each SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE change, while 1.27.2-0 and every later build (1.27.2-0 to 1.27.4-18) keep each stream's window as a delta from a connection-level initial window, so a change does constant work, as upstream Go 1.27.2 does. From the http2 tree, the golang.org/x/net copy vendored under src/vendor in these packages carries only the http2/hpack subpackage, not the golang.org/x/net/http2 package the module advisory names, and src/cmd/vendor carries no golang.org/x/net code, so the matched golang.org/x/net versions add no separate exposure. In every build the go command links the affected net/http/internal/http2 code (clientConnReadLoop.processSettingsNoWrite, clientConnReadLoop.processWindowUpdate and clientStream.awaitFlowControl appear in its Go function table), and the standard library source in the package is what Go programs built with it compile in. We also checked the golang-1.27-dev-oci-config, golang-1.27-dev-fips-oci-config (from the DHI security repository) and golang-1.27-dev-dbgsym (debug symbol) packages built from the same source; with the main packages that is 200 packages in all, each matching the repository index checksum, and the subpackages carry no other copy of net/http. The range ends at 1.27.2-0.
